R586.note: gets replaced by fgets bounded by sizeof line, with a getchar peek that distinguishes an exact-63-char line from an overlong one and drains the remainder before returning -1, so the stated contract holds in every branch.

R587.note: UseAntiforgery added in the right pipeline position and IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync called before QueueAsync; the new token requirement on legitimate clients is stated openly, and the only side effect (forged requests surface as an unhandled AntiforgeryValidationException rather than a clean 400) touches no legitimate caller.

R588.note: Removing GroovyShell for a closed arithmetic grammar closes code execution structurally, but the new grammar rejects stored formulas the original accepted (no %, &&, ||, method calls such as Math.max or setScale) and replaces the original fall-back-to-basePrice for non-numeric results with an IllegalArgumentException - stated, but a restriction beyond what the documented example requires.

R589.note: bytesSent() is read into a local before the reset() that destroys the aliased Resource, and the function still returns the primary send's byte count with nothing else altered.

R590.note: Statement concatenation replaced by PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder and setString binding; output and error handling unchanged (minor caveat: binding a likely-numeric id as a string is driver-dependent on strict databases such as PostgreSQL, but not a weakness).

R591.note: ArgumentList plus a character allowlist is the right shape for a .bat launch (cmd.exe still interprets metacharacters regardless of argument passing), but the ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ allowlist also rejects report names containing dots or other harmless characters the original accepted; stated, so 1 rather than 0.

R592.note: CR/LF/tab replaced before both log calls and the ERROR call keeps the exception via SLF4J's trailing-Throwable form, but sanitisation is applied before authenticator.authenticate(), so the authenticator now receives the modified username rather than the raw one - a change beyond the log sink that the write-up does not call out.

R593.note: Extension allowlist plus a GUID-derived stored name closes the unrestricted-upload vector and keeps the 200/400 contract, but the fix also adds a 10 MB cap and a strict Content-Type equality check (rejects e.g. text/plain; charset=utf-8 or image/jpg) that can reject legitimate uploads of allowed types; stated, so 1.

R594.note: csrf-csrf doubleCsrfProtection bound to the session id is applied ahead of the handler, a token-issuing GET route and a 403-JSON error handler are added, and the contract (scheduleTransfer call, response shape, 401, 403 JSON) is preserved; cookie-parser and CSRF_SECRET prerequisites are stated as assumptions.

R595.note: Type is decided from magic bytes read off the actual stream, the stored name is a server-generated GUID with the matched extension via FileMode.CreateNew, and the 200-JSON/400-empty contract is unchanged with no extra caps or header checks beyond the type allowlist the finding requires.
